candidates.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
candidates.title_zh: 隐式动力学的分层世界模型
candidates.abstract: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io
candidates.summary_zh: 提出ID-WM分层世界模型，将状态可达性与局部控制解耦：高层采样可行子目标，低层作为逆动力学求解器生成精确动作，从而提升长程规划与泛化。
candidates.contribution_zh: 解耦高层可达性与低层控制，用逆动力学世界模型落地子目标，缓解累积误差并在导航与操作任务显著提升。

ai_review.reason: 面向具身智能的分层世界模型与规划，直接服务机器人长程控制，范围契合。

candidates.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
candidates.title_zh: CausalWAM：学习世界动作模型中动作的因果来源
candidates.abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn latent variables from observations and use these to both predict the evolution of the scene and to generate actions. The prediction has to be of the whole scene, whereas only a portion of the scene causes actions. WAMs fitted to demonstrations do not, in general, guarantee that they will generate actions solely from the latent causes of the demonstrated actions (the action-relevant latent variables), as the model could just as well learn to imitate in this way whilst entangling the action-relevant latent variables with the nuisance variables. We therefore separate out what causes action from what prediction depends on. We prove that under a sparsity constraint the latent variables used to generate actions are an invertible function of the action-relevant latent variables alone and the true structure is identified up to a permutation of the latent variables. This requires neither sufficient temporal dependence nor any assumptions on how the unobserved regimes evolve and holds even when the action-relevant latent variables are statistically dependent on the rest. We therefore propose CWAM (Causal WAM), which incorporates the constraint into a pretrained WAM by adding a sparse routing path to its action head, with the world modeling objective remaining unchanged. Experiments on both synthetic data and real-world robots validate the theory as well as showcase the improved efficiency in closed-loop success.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出因果世界动作模型CWAM，将动作相关潜变量与场景预测潜变量分离，在预训练WAM动作头加入稀疏路由约束，实现动作因果结构可识别，并在合成数据与真实机器人上验证闭环效率提升。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将稀疏路由约束引入预训练世界动作模型的策略头，理论证明动作相关潜变量可识别，并提升真实机器人闭环任务效率。

ai_review.reason: 研究机器人世界动作模型的因果潜变量与动作生成，含理论证明及真实机器人验证，直接相关。

candidates.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
candidates.title_zh: 测试时搜索何时帮助世界动作模型？候选选择与仿真器完整性的实证审计
candidates.abstract: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.
candidates.summary_zh: 预注册审计世界动作模型的测试时搜索：学习价值选择器劣于随机，预言机增益仅1.40pp；token剪枝端到端加速至多1.15倍；并发现修复静默渲染损坏。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示测试时扩展需按决策信号、实际效率与评估完整性逐项审计，并提供渲染损坏检测器、修复与脚本。

ai_review.reason: 直接研究世界动作模型的测试时搜索、候选选择与仿真器完整性，属具身智能与机器人评估范围

candidates.title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
candidates.title_zh: 当仿真器而非策略失败：审计仿真机器人基准中的接触伪影
candidates.abstract: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文提出 SimuGuard，审计 LIBERO、RoboTwin 等机器人仿真基准中的接触伪影，定位物理引擎三角面阈值导致的物体弹飞，并修复后提升成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示仿真接触失败源于引擎碰撞检测常数，提供可复现审计插件并量化成功率偏差。

ai_review.reason: 直接分析机器人仿真物理引擎接触伪影及基准评测，属于物理智能评测基础设施。

candidates.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
candidates.title_zh: 当过去塑造行动：理解具身记忆
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.
candidates.summary_zh: 系统综述具身记忆：把记忆视为在当前观测之外保留决策相关信息的功能，按六类记忆需求与八类架构（循环状态、快速权重、视觉与符号表示、空间记忆、经验系统）梳理方法、能力与局限，并评述依赖记忆的基准测试，指出经验选择、信念一致性与跨回合知识固化等开放问题。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出以六项记忆需求与八类架构构成的二维分类框架，区分基准中真实的历史信息使用与一般任务表现，为具身智能体的记忆设计提供统一分析视角。

ai_review.reason: 具身记忆综述，直接服务机器人长程任务与决策，属具身智能范畴

candidates.title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
candidates.title_zh: VLA策略不知道何时不应行动：非预期任务执行与启动抑制
candidates.abstract: A robot should act only on an instruction from a person or on an intent that the robot explicitly represents and generates. Unintended actions taken without such an instruction can cause risk or inconvenience to people and the environment. We examine how recent vision-language-action (VLA) policies respond when the instruction is missing or meaningless. We apply a paired protocol with empty, neutral, nonsense, infeasible, and wrong-task instructions to six model checkpoints in LIBERO-Goal simulation. Holding the initial state fixed and varying only the instruction, we ask three questions: whether the robot starts to move, which task it completes, and what the instruction determines. Even when the instruction was empty, the robot started moving in every episode with all six checkpoints, and with five of them it often completed a task that the instruction had not specified. On two GR00T checkpoints, the instruction determined which task was executed but not whether the robot started moving; the robot moved even on infeasible instructions. We then tested three methods for suppressing the start: prepending "if no task is given do not move" to the instruction; a gate that holds the robot when the first action chunk for the given instruction nearly equals that for an empty instruction; and fine-tuning the policy to hold still on non-task inputs. The prefix stopped the robot in none of the six checkpoints, and the gate held it on non-task inputs in five of the six checkpoints. The fine-tuned policy never completed a task on non-task inputs, but it did not reliably keep the robot still, and it failed to suppress the start on infeasible instructions.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文在LIBERO-Goal配对测试六种VLA检查点对空、中性、无意义、不可行及错误指令的反应，发现无指令仍常启动并执行未指定任务，并评估三种启动抑制方法。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示VLA策略缺乏“不行动”判断，比较提示、动作门控与微调对误启动的抑制效果。

ai_review.reason: 直接研究VLA策略在缺失或无意义指令下的误执行与启动抑制，属具身智能与机器人安全。

candidates.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: SACQ：面向超低位视觉-语言-动作模型的结构感知码本量化
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable capable robot behavior, but their large memory footprint limits deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Weight quantization is a natural remedy, yet post-training quantization (PTQ) recipes inherited from large language models degrade when applied to VLAs at ultra-low precision. Existing low-bit PTQ methods often fail to explicitly account for the structure of downstream operations and allocate precision without considering its effect on the policy actions. We introduce SACQ, an ultra- low-bit weight-only vector-codebook quantization framework for VLAs. SACQ combines (1) structure-aware codebook fitting with role-specific quadratic metrics that reflect input statistics and downstream sensitivity; (2) action-aware mixed-bit allocation based on the increase in final-action error as individual layers are compressed; and (3) two-stage post-quantization refinement that reassigns codeword indices with second-order error compensation and calibrates codebooks and row-group scales against the decoded action. Using GR00T N1.7, SACQ achieves 93.85% average success across four LIBERO suites at 1.5 bits per language/action weight while reducing model memory by 4.83x. With INT8 activation quantization and low-precision attention, it retains 93.55% success while running 1.51x faster than BF16. On SimplER, SACQ further achieves 63.76% and 52.27% success under Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation at 2 bits per language/action weight, compared to 58.90% and 53.45% for BF16, respectively.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出SACQ，一种仅权重的超低位向量码本量化框架，结合结构感知码本拟合、动作感知混合位宽分配与两阶段后量化细化，降低VLA内存并保持机器人操作成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 设计结构感知与动作敏感的低位码本量化及混合精度分配，在GR00T N1.7等VLA上实现约4.83倍内存压缩并保持高任务成功率。

ai_review.reason: 面向VLA机器人模型的超低位量化，直接服务资源受限平台部署，属具身智能范围。

candidates.title: Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning by Coupling Body-Agnostic World Model with Differentiable Ego-Dynamics
candidates.title_zh: 以体无关世界模型耦合可微自运动动力学的跨本体运动规划
candidates.abstract: Motion planning in clutter is embodiment-specific: the feasible free space and reachable commands depend on each robot's geometry and dynamics. Existing cross-embodiment policies output normalized commands that disregard these differences, or compensate through per-robot training and distillation. World models can in principle pool cross-embodiment data, yet command-conditioned models bind their latent dynamics to a single action space, while pose-conditioned models omit the mapping from commands to body-specific motion. On flat ground, however, embodiment affects the planner's observations only through the camera ego-motion. This letter proposes Hourglass, an hourglass-shaped architecture that factorizes cross-embodiment motion planning at this interface: a body-agnostic world model and each robot's differentiable ego-dynamics, which map commands to that ego-motion, are coupled only through it. The world model is trained on data pooled across embodiments and camera mounts; each robot's ego-dynamics is a reduced-order template with identified physical parameters. A generalist parameter-conditioned policy is learned once at this junction: each imagined step rolls out the template and then the world model, and imagination training through each robot's template makes the policy body-aware. On seven simulated robots of five locomotion types, the generalist policy outperforms imitation-learning and diffusion-policy baselines on the same world model by 3.8--10.6 percentage points in success rate and matches per-robot specialists without dedicated training, while approaching its parameter-conditioned MPPI teacher within 1.4--2.8 points without an online map. After three minutes of teleoperated driving for identification, the synthetic-data-trained model transfers zero-shot to a real skid-steer robot unseen in training, navigating unseen indoor scenes.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出沙漏式架构：体无关世界模型与各机器人可微自运动动力学仅通过相机自运动接口耦合，在共享数据上训练通用参数条件策略，七种仿真机器人上超越模仿与扩散基线并零样本迁移到真实机器人。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将跨本体规划分解为体无关世界模型与可微本体动力学，经想象训练得到本体感知的通用规划策略。

ai_review.reason: 提出跨本体世界模型与可微自运动动力学耦合的规划框架，属机器人世界模型与规划核心范畴
